routing.reason: Accounts, sessions and per-user task ownership touch the DB schema, API, auth and the page, in a small codebase with fully testable acceptance criteria.
rulings: Ruling: default workflow, not direct — the ticket is security sensitive (authentication, passwords, tokens, access rights) and spans back end and page — cost if wrong: direct would skip the plan gate and the security review.
Ruling: product owner skipped (frame off) — the nine acceptance criteria are already testable and precise — cost if wrong: a missed edge case would surface only at review.

Ruling: PM, architect, UX and SEO left off — the design is settled by the criteria (scrypt, hashed random tokens, owner column), the page is a small form added to the existing one, and no public pages change — cost if wrong: front may need one rework for the form's states.

Ruling: security review at high effort — passwords, session tokens, authorization on every task route and a hard no-leak rule — cost if wrong: a flaw in authentication or cross-user access would ship.
Ruling: no squads — the project declares none; the lead plans back (migration, users, sessions, ownership, tests), front (page), and docs (README) as roles — cost if wrong: none.

Ruling: guidance for the plan — add a new migration (never edit the shipped one) with users, sessions (token hash only) and a nullable tasks.user_id so old tasks stay but match no user; scope every task query by user_id so a foreign task answers the same 404 as a missing one; malformed JSON on the new routes should answer 400, not 500 — cost if wrong: rework of the migration or an information leak between users.
Ruling: budget $2.50 (the cap) — M work with a plan, implementation, review rounds and a high-effort security review — cost if wrong: a lower budget could stop the run before its reviews.

criteria.why: createUser lowercases, validates with /^[a-z0-9_]{3,32}$/, 10-char password check, 409 on duplicate (with UNIQUE race handling), 201 {id, username}.
POST /api/sessions returns 201 {token}; unknown user and wrong password both give 401 invalid credentials, with a dummy scrypt for equal cost.
All /api/tasks and /api/tasks/* routes check the bearer token first and answer 401 authentication required.
All task queries are scoped by user_id; other users' tasks give the same 404 as missing ones, and tests cover it.
DELETE /api/sessions deletes the token hash and answers 204; unknown or missing token gives 401, and tests cover it.
Scrypt with a per-user salt and timingSafeEqual; 32 random bytes for the token, with SHA-256 stored; no hash is returned, and a test inspects the DB and responses.
The migration adds user_id as NULL; queries filter by user_id, so legacy rows are invisible, and a migration test covers it.
The page has sign-in and sign-up forms, sends the Bearer token on every request, and has a sign-out button.
New accounts test file, existing tests updated to sign in, README documents accounts and auth.

findings.what: readJson accumulates the whole body with no size limit, and scrypt runs on unbounded password length. Both are DoS vectors on the unauthenticated /api/users and /api/sessions routes.
Sessions never expire and no cleanup exists. The README admits this, but it is a weakness for a security-sensitive ticket.
createUser checks 'username taken' before it runs scrypt, so a client can enumerate usernames. The ticket requires the 409, so this is acceptable.
The title is not validated. The test even expects a 500 for a missing title, which hides a validation gap. The gap is pre-existing but surfaced here.
Changes to 500 handling (generic message and logging), a new invalid-JSON 400 and the HttpError class go beyond the ticket. They are reasonable hardening but unrequested.
Extra UI machinery (session-ended handling, render race guard, button disabling, error mapping) goes beyond the minimal forms. The token is kept in sessionStorage.
There is no UI test, and the 'authentication before method' test enshrines an ordering the ticket does not require.

judge.summary: The diff meets all nine criteria with correct scrypt hashing, hashed tokens, per-user scoping on every query, and thorough tests covering each criterion, including migration and no-leak checks. Weaknesses are no body or password size limit on the public auth routes, sessions that never expire, and some unrequested extras (500 and JSON-error handling, UI polish).
